findings.title: Standard HTTP/HTTPS Ports Open
findings.description: The target exposes standard HTTP (80) and HTTPS (443) ports, indicating a typical web server setup.
findings.recommendation: Ensure all web services are properly secured and patched.

findings.title: Exposed Login Page
findings.description: A public-facing login page was identified, which could be vulnerable to brute-force attacks or credential stuffing.
findings.recommendation: Implement strong authentication mechanisms, rate limiting, and multi-factor authentication.

findings.title: Missing Security Headers
findings.description: Several important security headers, including X-Frame-Options, X-XSS-Protection, and X-Content-Type-Options, are missing.
findings.recommendation: Implement all recommended security headers to mitigate common client-side attacks.

findings.title: SQL Injection Vulnerability
findings.description: The 'id' GET parameter appears vulnerable to boolean-based blind SQL injection, potentially allowing unauthorized data access.
findings.recommendation: Implement parameterized queries or prepared statements to prevent SQL injection.

findings.title: Default or Weak Credentials Found
findings.description: Default or easily guessable credentials were found for an administrative login page, leading to unauthorized access.
findings.recommendation: Enforce strong, unique passwords for all accounts and implement multi-factor authentication.
findings.poc: hydra -L users.txt -P passwords.txt example.com http-post-form "/admin/login.php:user=^USER^&pass=^PASS^:F=Login Failed"

findings.title: Strong TLS Protocols and Ciphers
findings.description: The server supports modern TLS versions (1.2, 1.3) and strong cipher suites.
findings.recommendation: Regularly review and update TLS configurations to maintain optimal security.

findings.title: Exposed Development Subdomain
findings.description: A 'dev' subdomain was identified, which often contains sensitive information or outdated code.
findings.recommendation: Secure or remove development environments that are publicly accessible.

findings.title: CORS Wildcard Misconfiguration
findings.description: The API endpoint allows all origins with credentials, enabling malicious cross-site data theft.
findings.recommendation: Restrict CORS 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' to a specific list of trusted domains.

findings.title: Publicly Writable S3 Bucket
findings.description: An S3 bucket is configured for public read and write access, allowing unauthorized data manipulation or storage.
findings.recommendation: Restrict S3 bucket permissions to only authorized users and services.

findings.title: Critical Vulnerabilities in Container Image
findings.description: The application container image contains critical vulnerabilities, including RCE in Nginx, posing significant risk.
findings.recommendation: Update the base image and all installed packages to their latest patched versions.

findings.title: Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA)
findings.description: The API allows unauthorized access to other users' data by manipulating the user ID in the endpoint.
findings.recommendation: Implement strict authorization checks at the API endpoint to ensure users can only access their own resources.

findings.title: AWS Access Key Leak in Backup File
findings.description: An AWS Access Key ID was discovered in a publicly accessible backup configuration file, posing a severe compromise risk.
findings.recommendation: Immediately revoke the exposed AWS key and ensure sensitive files are not publicly accessible.

findings.title: Cloudflare WAF Detected
findings.description: The target website is protected by Cloudflare WAF, providing a layer of security against common web attacks.
findings.recommendation: Understand WAF rules and continuously test for potential bypasses.

findings.title: Exposed SMB Share with Weak Credentials
findings.description: An internal SMB share was found with weak or default credentials, allowing unauthorized access to sensitive files.
findings.recommendation: Restrict SMB access to internal networks only and enforce strong authentication for all shares.

findings.title: Subdomain Takeover Vulnerability
findings.description: A subdomain is pointing to a dangling DNS record, allowing an attacker to claim the service and host malicious content.
findings.recommendation: Remove the dangling DNS record or claim the associated service to prevent subdomain takeover.

agents.command: msfconsole -q -x "use auxiliary/scanner/http/http_login..." && hydra -L users.txt example.com http-post-form
amass enum -passive -d example.com && theHarvester -d example.com -b all
python3 cors_scanner.py -u https://example.com && python3 ssrf_scanner.py -u https://example.com
kr scan https://example.com -w routes-large.kite && restler --target https://example.com
cme smb example.com -u '' -p '' && bloodhound-python -d example.com -u null -p null -c All
subzy run --targets subdomains.txt && nuclei -tags takeover -u https://example.com
